ui_bugs.issue: After ws-disconnect, selecting another category correctly re-fetches data (RouterOS pool reconnects server-side) but the 'No session' text stays until the 15s interval polls /connection. Should call loadConn() after each ResourceTable fetch (or lift connection polling to a shorter interval / event-based).

design_issues.screen: Overview traffic chart on first render inside workspace transitions
issues: Recharts warns 'width(-1) and height(-1)' during route changes (harmless but noisy)

action_items: Optional: refresh WorkspacePage connection indicator immediately after resource fetches so 'Session up' reflects the reconnect without waiting 15s
Carry-over from iter-8: probe_router() still doesn't populate memory; ppp-toggle spacing; cascade-delete for router-owned data
critical_code_review_comments: App.js is now 518 lines with 400+ char single-line JSX (line 497, 503, 508, 510) — split Sidebar/Topbar/GroupsView/AlarmsView/RoutersTable into components; readability + testability suffer.

server.py: _ROS_POOLS is a module-level dict guarded by threading.Lock but each ros_call runs in a separate asyncio.to_thread — concurrent reads for the same router can race on pool.get_api() (only one pool.disconnect on failure, but simultaneous first-time calls both call _new_pool). Consider a per-router asyncio.Lock or double-check inside the lock in _get_pool_entry.

server.py delete_group only checks db.routers by exact-match {'group': name} — does not warn if the group is referenced only in DEMO['routers']; acceptable because demo groups are also in DEMO['groups'] and blocked by the 400 path, but worth an explicit comment.
GroupCreate has no trim() at schema level; server strips manually — pattern check could prevent whitespace-only names.
WorkspacePage doesn't call loadConn() after each resource load, so indicator lags reality (see UI bug above).

The window.location URL parse in App.js is one-shot on data.routers.length change; if user reloads while URL already has a matching router but data hasn't loaded yet, the effect only fires once — works today because loadOverview is the sole populator.
